description: On the production server, a PDF export never prints a character of the letter or CV as a missing-glyph box; hyphens such as the one in "decade‑long" print as hyphens.

userStories.title: The cover letter PDF prints every hyphen and punctuation mark
userStories.description: As a user downloading my cover letter as a PDF, I want every hyphen, dash and space in my text to print as it does in the editor, so that the letter I send has no crossed boxes in it.
acceptanceCriteria: A cover letter containing every character of the FR-2 set (in the opening, body and closing), downloaded as PDF from the serverless runtime, shows no missing-glyph box on its rendered page. This is checked on the rendered page image, for Georgia, and for paragraphs in Arial and in Calibri.

In that PDF: "decade‑long" written with U+2010, with U+2011 and with U+002D prints a visible hyphen between "decade" and "long" in all three cases; the PDF text extracts "decade" and "long" with a hyphen character between them.
A line never breaks right after a U+2011, in the PDF as in the editor. The check is a line long enough that it would wrap there if the character could break.
A U+00AD prints nothing on a line that does not break at it.
A letter with no character of the FR-2 set prints a PDF identical in text, line breaks and page count to the current output, on both the local and the serverless runtime.
The cover letter Word export of the same letter contains each FR-2 character as written. It is opened in Microsoft Word, and no box shows.
FR-1: On the serverless runtime, no character of a letter or CV prints as a missing-glyph box when it is in a substitute face's registered `unicode-range` but has no glyph in that face.

FR-2: The verification set is: U+00AD soft hyphen; U+2010 hyphen; U+2011 non-breaking hyphen; U+2012 figure dash; U+2015 horizontal bar; U+2020 dagger; U+2021 double dagger; U+2030 per mille; U+2032 prime; U+202F narrow no-break space. Also checked as controls, already correct today: U+002D, U+2013, U+2014, U+2022 and U+00A0.

FR-3: The hyphens U+2010, U+2011 and U+2012 print with the width of the font's own hyphen. This keeps the substitutes' metric compatibility, so a line with them breaks where the user's own print breaks it.
FR-4: U+2011 keeps its no-break meaning, and U+202F keeps its no-break meaning. U+00AD stays invisible unless the line breaks at it.

FR-5: An automated check fails when a substitute face is registered for a code point it has no glyph for, unless that code point is handled by the FR-1 fix. A Fontsource update that changes coverage must fail the check, not print boxes.
FR-6: The fix applies to both PDF renderers through one shared mechanism. There is no cover-letter-only or resume-only variant.
FR-7: Stored text and the Word exports are unchanged.
Regression constraint: On the local runtime (developer machines, the e2e suite) the PDFs print exactly as today: the real Georgia, Arial and Calibri are used, and no substitute is registered.
Regression constraint: On the serverless runtime, text without FR-2 characters prints with the same substitutes, line breaks and page count as today.

Regression constraint: The renderer's isolation is not weakened: no network request for fonts beyond those the resume renderer already makes (Google Fonts); fonts stay inline `data:` sources from installed packages; the cover letter page keeps scripts off and every request aborted.
Regression constraint: The cover letter's 816 × 1056 px page, margins and paging, and the resumes' A4 output, are unchanged.
Regression constraint: Parity stays at MATCH 211 / KNOWN 3 / NEW 0, and the visual suite stays unchanged.
Verification: All checks of CLAUDE.md §14: typecheck, test, test:integration, test:e2e, build, lint (≤ the tracked 286), and test:parity.
Verification: Unit: the FR-5 coverage check, run against the installed Fontsource files.

Verification: Serverless evidence (export-validation): PDFs of US-001 and US-002 fixtures generated on the branch's Vercel Preview deployment, or on a local reproduction that registers the same substitutes and has only Open Sans as a system font. If the reproduction is used, its faithfulness must be shown, by reproducing the box with the current code before the fix. Each PDF is rasterized and inspected for boxes; Its text is extracted; The before/after line breaks and page count are compared for a fixture with no FR-2 characters.
Verification: Word: the cover letter and resume .docx are opened in Microsoft Word with the FR-2 set (US-001, US-002).
Verification: Security: security-review if the change touches the renderer's page setup, font loading or request policy.
FAIL condition: Any FR-2 character prints as a box in any checked font, in a PDF from the serverless runtime.
FAIL condition: "decade‑long" with U+2010 or U+2011 prints without a visible hyphen, or its extracted text lacks the hyphen.
FAIL condition: A line breaks after a U+2011, or a U+00AD shows on a line that does not break at it.
FAIL condition: A PDF without FR-2 characters changes its text, line breaks or page count on either runtime.
FAIL condition: Stored text is modified, or the Word exports change.
FAIL condition: The fix works only in the cover letter or only in the resume renderer (FR-6).
FAIL condition: The local-runtime e2e passes but no serverless evidence exists.
BLOCKER condition: No serverless evidence can be produced: no Vercel Preview deployment for the branch and no faithful local reproduction.

BLOCKER condition: No font available to the serverless renderer, installed or from an installed package, can draw a hyphen of the same width as the substitute's own hyphen, and the only remaining way is to change the text as printed.
BLOCKER condition: The Word check shows the same defect in a Word export (scope decision for the owner).
Out of scope: Changing stored letters or CVs, or rewriting characters when the user types or saves them.
Out of scope: Changing the editor, the Preview, or the fonts the user picks.
Out of scope: Replacing the substitutes (Gelasio, Arimo, Carlito) or the serverless Chromium.
Out of scope: Scripts other than Latin (Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese subsets), except that the change must not break them.
Out of scope: Word export changes, unless the Word check finds the same defect (then it is a BLOCKER for an owner decision, not silent extra scope).
